area: web app / Sanctuary site / CLI (plus the ERC-4804 on-chain renderer and the unmerged Sanctuary Commons branch)
summary:
ANIMA has three human surfaces delivered three ways. (1) The Sanctuary (index.html + src/main.js 26,881 B + src/style.css 17,569 B) is a Vite single-page app published to GitHub Pages by .github/workflows/pages.yml, loading Google Fonts; it is not on chain. It targets Base Sepolia ANIMA 0xb3d92c766e3cb356db381feb21958a9ebb974365 over the public RPC https://sepolia.base.org with a hand-written viem ABI subset, offers Connect wallet / mint / inspect-by-id, and a 'command chamber' console with setStatus and deployAccount, wallet_watchAsset, and a self-contained data:application/json + data:image/svg+xml metadata built client-side at mint. Ownership verification is purely client-side enumeration: after eth_requestAccounts it reads totalMinted() and calls ownerOf(id) for every id, keeping the ones equal to the connected address (src/main.js:178); there is no signature challenge, no SIWE and no server, and the only real gate is the token contract's own authorisation surfaced via simulateContract before signing. (2) contracts/web/AnimaWeb3Renderer.sol is a stateless, ownerless ERC-4804 manual-mode contract whose fallback(bytes path) returns ABI-encoded HTML for /token/{id}/live (web3://0x9160bE4d…:84532/token/{id}/live, or the w3link gateway). It is the only UI served from chain: 22,592 runtime bytes (1,984 under EIP-170), ~15.8 KB of literal HTML/CSS/JS per page, four tabs (overview, identity, control, advanced raw-call console), no viewer gating, and writes authorised by the contract via simulate-then-sign. Its fatal flaw for the GOAL is that the embedded module script imports viem from https://esm.sh/viem@2.55.19, and it hard-codes RPC/explorer for two chains and mislabels the six-value SealPolicy enum with three strings. (3) cli/anima.mjs is a readline wizard that binds an ENS name to an agent: it requires isController(agentId, signer), writes addr/com.anima.agent/com.anima.account/url/contenthash atomically via resolver multicall, and optionally transfers .eth custody into the agent's ERC-6551 account only for mainnet-homed agents and only if the signer is ownerOf; it pins the GUI as an IPFS CID in ENS contenthash.

The machine-discovery surface (public/.well-known/anima.json, llms.txt, the generated 29-contract/657-function anima-functions.json, the strict ERC-8004 registration-v1 manifest schema with a gui block, and the example manifest that advertises the renderer as the agent GUI) is well designed and schema-tested (test/ManifestSchema.test.mjs). The deployment tooling (scripts/deploy-web3-renderer.ts with web3RendererHistory, testnet-batch-mint.ts with checkpoints and RPC-lag defences, testnet-batch-exercise.ts with a 32-tx read-back audit) is solid and reusable as patterns.

The unmerged branch upgrade/sanctuary-commons-3d-20260904 is the only messaging/social work in the repo: AnimaCommons.sol (12,941 B; circles, invitations, moderators, bans, two-step stewardship, slow mode, 1,024-byte posts, revisions, tombstones, reactions, accepted replies, exact-hash WorkEscrow links, fingerprint-pinned agent badges, a domain-separated history root), 29 contract tests passing on both token builds (322 total), plus a 50 KB SPA with a dependency-free WebGL scene, a block-pinned bounded-read bridge with epoch-guarded simulate/review/re-simulate/commit, and Playwright checks executing real transactions on a loopback Hardhat EVM. It was never deployed and explicitly refuses to claim the ~443 KB client is on chain.

Verdicts: keep and harden the ERC-4804 renderer (remove esm.sh, split into router + module pages because of EIP-170, add controller/role-aware gating in the client); adapt the Sanctuary's wallet/mint/console flows but drop the static page, fictional data, O(n) ownership scan and CDN fonts; reuse the CLI's contenthash/custody helpers and adapt the wizard to web3:// targets; adapt AnimaCommons as the social contract and the bridge/model safety patterns; drop the 3D scene and the GitHub Pages pipeline. Two concrete bugs to not inherit: the Sanctuary commits manifestHash = keccak256(uriString) rather than of the served bytes, and neither transact nor mintAgent checks receipt.status.

Hard-coded Base Sepolia (0xb3d92c76…, switched from 0x0aeb6f78… in commit 9cb1ebb) and a single public RPC; vite base './' so one build works on localhost, IPFS directory and GitHub Pages.

components.name: AnimaWeb3Renderer (ERC-4804 manual-mode on-chain console)
components.purpose: Stateless, ownerless contract that serves a complete HTML/CSS/JS agent console for /token/{id}/live from current ANIMA state, reachable via web3:// or a w3link gateway; the only UI in the repo delivered from chain.
key_functions: constructor(IAnimaWeb3View anima_) — reverts ZeroAddress() on 0 (:26-29)
function resolveMode() external pure returns (bytes32) — bytes32('manual') (:32-34)

fallback(bytes calldata path) external returns (bytes memory) — '/' -> index; '/token/<digits>/live' -> try ownerOf -> token page with ownerOf/accountOf; else not-found; always abi.encode(string) (:37-47)
_tokenPath(bytes) private pure returns (bool, uint256) — prefix/suffix byte compare, decimal parse without overflow guard (:49-64)
_token(id, owner, account) — header/chain pill/#connect; main#app data-token/data-contract/data-chain=block.chainid; tabs overview/identity/control/advanced (:76-99)

_script() — <script type=module> importing viem from https://esm.sh/viem@2.55.19; rpc map {11155111, 84532}; 14-entry ABI; refresh(); connect(); send(fn,args) simulate->write->wait->refresh; raw parseAbiItem console (:126-137)
IAnimaWeb3View { ownerOf(uint256); accountOf(uint256) } (:6-9)
design_decisions: NatSpec (:11-17): 'A Web3URL client sends the URL path as raw fallback calldata. The fallback response is an ABI-encoded string, as required by manual mode. Keeping this separate from the immutable ANIMA diamond lets an existing collection gain a browser without changing token logic.'

deploy script (:36-37): 'The renderer is immutable, stateless and has no privileged owner. Any funded account may deploy it, which makes recovery possible without the original collection deployer key.'

Configuration is read from data-* attributes so one bytecode serves any chain; three iterations in one day (2d74176 static view -> 9cb1ebb link to GitHub Pages -> 20bfda6 full console) and test now asserts doesNotMatch(/github\.io/).
security_invariants: No state, no owner, no events; every response is a view over the token contract.
All writes are simulated with account:user before the wallet is asked to sign; authorisation is entirely the token contract's.
components.reuse_notes: The keeper. Must remove the esm.sh import (embed or SSTORE2 a minimal coder, or use the wallet provider as transport), fix the 3-of-6 seal labels at :131, drop hard-coded RPC/explorer maps, add controller/role-aware client gating, and split into router + per-module page contracts: 22,592/24,576 bytes used, so swap/launchpad/vault/messaging cannot fit here.

standards_implemented: ERC-4804 manual mode (resolveMode + fallback path routing) in AnimaWeb3Renderer
ERC-721 / ERC-6551 / ERC-5646 reads from the UIs
ERC-8004 registration-v1 manifest shape with anima extension (schema, example, SDK types)
ENS addr/text/contenthash (EIP-1577 ipfs-ns 0xe3) via resolver multicall; NameWrapper and BaseRegistrar custody
EIP-712 AgentWalletBinding in the batch-exercise script
ERC-721 metadata as self-contained data: URI with data:image/svg+xml image (client-generated)
unique_ideas: A separate, stateless, ownerless ERC-4804 renderer contract that gives an already-immutable token collection a browser without touching token logic, re-deployable by any key (recovery after the deployer key was destroyed).
Configuration injected via data-token/data-contract/data-chain attributes so one renderer bytecode serves any chain; three renderer iterations archived in web3RendererHistory.
ADVANCED tab: user types any Solidity function signature + JSON args; page parses with parseAbiItem, simulates, then asks the wallet — a generic on-chain console with simulate-before-sign.
Self-contained data:application/json + data:image/svg+xml token metadata built at mint so wallets need no server/IPFS.

ENS binding of an agent: addr -> ERC-6551 account, text com.anima.agent = eip155:chain:contract:id, optional transfer of the .eth NFT into the agent account so the name follows token ownership (mainnet-only, owner-only, typed confirmation).

Manifest commitment over exact served bytes (keccak256 of the response, hash before parse), strict schema with a declarative gui block, and a machine-readable .well-known directory plus a full ABI/selector index for agents.

AnimaCommons: fingerprint-pinned agent badges (controller + ERC-5646 state at publication), tombstones that admit they cannot delete, exact-spec-hash links to escrow jobs, per-circle hash-chained history root, byte-counted limits, two-step stewardship.
CommonsBridge: all reads in a view pinned to one block number, bounded pagination, epoch-guarded review and re-simulation immediately before send, config/chain/binding verification before any write.
Loopback JSON-RPC proxy with a method allowlist over Hardhat's in-process EVM plus a Playwright EIP-1193 shim so browser tests execute real transactions.
weaknesses: The user-facing website is a GitHub Pages static bundle with Google Fonts; the on-chain renderer imports viem from https://esm.sh (AnimaWeb3Renderer.sol:128), so no surface is actually dependency-free.

Renderer: seal labels wrong (3 strings for 6 enum values, :131); RPC/explorer hard-coded for 84532/11155111 (:129); 22,592/24,576 bytes used so no room for module UIs; capability chips are badges with no functionality; _tokenPath decimal parse has no overflow guard.

Sanctuary: ownership = O(totalMinted) concurrent ownerOf calls with silent per-id failures (:178); only ownerOf, not isController/roles/leases; receipt.status never checked (:180-181); manifestHash = keccak256(uriString) not of served bytes (:181) so verifyManifest fails; fictional bond/trust/'231 proofs' marketing data; external_url bakes the GitHub Pages URL into on-chain metadata.

Address and documentation drift: src/main.js and .well-known target ANIMA 0xb3d92c76… (deployer 0xc591…) while README step 5, CLAUDE.md, deployments/84532.json and the commons branch describe 0x0aeb6f78… (deployer key destroyed); deploy-web3-renderer.yml defaults to the 0x0aeb record.

No UI tests on main; CI does not run test:cli, test:manifest-schema, test:diamond or the Vite build; test counts drift between README (279), CLAUDE.md (268), commit 697df74 (235) and the commons branch (322).
CLI pins the GUI as an IPFS CID in ENS contenthash (contradicts a no-IPFS goal), .eth only, interactive path untested.
AnimaCommons is unaudited, undeployed, public-only by design, Sybil-exposed reactions, and social principals are addresses that may themselves be transferable token-bound accounts.
Minting is permissionless on the token; the Sanctuary relies on it; no pricing/gating exists.
website_delivery: Primary human UI (the Sanctuary) is delivered from a centralised static host: Vite build of index.html + src/main.js + src/style.css published to GitHub Pages (https://venividis.github.io/Cutting-edge-technologically-advanced-NFT/) by .github/workflows/pages.yml, with fonts from Google Fonts; it is not on chain and not on IPFS, and the mint path bakes that URL into the token's external_url. A second UI is served from chain: contracts/web/AnimaWeb3Renderer.sol is an ERC-4804 manual-mode contract (resolveMode()=='manual') whose fallback(bytes path) returns abi.encode(string html) for '/', '/token/{id}/live' and a not-found page, reachable as web3://0x9160bE4d943516a2463Ac5f3ABAc5F5cce7975Cd:84532/token/{id}/live or via https://0x9160be4d943516a2463ac5f3abac5f5cce7975cd.basesep.w3link.io/token/{id}/live (public/.well-known/anima.json:60-64). The served page (~15.8 KB; contract runtime 22,592 B) carries its own CSS, markup and a <script type=module> that reads live state over a hard-coded public RPC and submits simulate-then-sign writes through window.ethereum — but that script imports viem from https://esm.sh/viem@2.55.19, so the on-chain page still depends on a CDN. The NFT's own tokenURI is a plain stored string (AnimaAgent.sol:360-363); the Sanctuary writes a self-contained data:application/json + data:image/svg+xml document into it at mint, so wallets render the NFT without a server, but no website is minted with the token. A third route, the CLI, pins a GUI as an IPFS CID in an ENS contenthash. The unmerged commons branch builds a ~443 KB standalone HTML client and explicitly states it is not deployed on chain.
wallet_gating: No surface uses a server, SIWE or a signature challenge. Sanctuary: connect() calls eth_requestAccounts and switches/adds Base Sepolia (src/main.js:179); discover() reads totalMinted() and calls ownerOf(id) for every id 1..total, treating ids whose owner equals the connected address as 'yours' (src/main.js:178); the owner console is then shown, but all writes (setStatus, deployAccount, mintAgent) are gated only by the token contract, surfaced through simulateContract({account}) before writeContract (src/main.js:180-181); anyone can inspect any token id without a wallet (src/main.js:187). On-chain renderer: no viewer gating at all — every visitor sees owner, ERC-6551 account and fingerprint for the token in the URL; CONNECT WALLET uses eth_requestAccounts + switchChain/wallet_addEthereumChain, and every control (deployAccount, setStatus 1/2/4, setGuardian, setOperator, arbitrary signature) is simulated with the connected account and then signed; a non-holder simply gets a simulation revert (AnimaWeb3Renderer.sol:133-135). CLI: refuses unless ANIMA.isController(agentId, signer) (cli/anima.mjs:119-125); permanent ENS custody additionally requires ownerOf(id)==signer, home chain 1, and retyping the name (:145-151). Commons branch: the wallet address is the social principal; an agent badge on a post requires isController plus an exact current getStateFingerprint, and the contract snapshots ownerOf at publication; the client's requireWrite() demands a verified deployment, explicit wallet connection and matching chain (bridge.js:37). None of the UIs recognises operators, ERC-4907 users, guardians or ERC-7432 roles when deciding what to show; the GOAL's 'holder or authorised by holder' check should be implemented client-side with isController/roles for display and left to the contracts for enforcement.

No tests cover src/main.js, src/style.css or the renderer's embedded JavaScript. tokenURI is an arbitrary controller-set string; the Brave-ready data: SVG metadata is a client convention, not a contract guarantee; manifestHash must be computed over the bytes the URI serves (the Sanctuary gets this wrong).
mintAgent is permissionless; the Sanctuary's one-click mint depends on that, and a unified protocol will need gating/pricing and a regenerated function index.

Public RPC lag: wait for code before constructors inspect fresh deployments, take ids from receipt logs, block until the endpoint reaches the receipt block (testnet-batch-mint.ts:132-140); the commons bridge also disables client caching after a real cache bug.
expectRevert in tests matches 4-byte selectors because facet errors cannot be decoded through the diamond; new tests must verify they are not vacuous.
